Zendesk.//Subdomain: The Zendesk account subdomain: 'acme' for https://acme.zendesk.com.
Zendesk.//KeyVaultUri: Holds the Zendesk OAuth client secret and one secret per connected person. The managed identity needs Key Vault Secrets Officer (it writes tokens).
Zendesk.//OAuthClientId: The Zendesk OAuth client's unique identifier (Admin Centre > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients).
Zendesk.//TokenSecretPrefix: Each person's token is stored as {prefix}{Entra object id}. Staging sets its own prefix so the targets never share a token.
Zendesk.//DevelopmentApiToken: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY, with OAuth:NoAuth=true and no KeyVaultUri: every call is made as DevelopmentEmail. The server refuses to start with it anywhere else.
Zendesk.//Features: Account-wide switches for the actions with the widest reach. All default to off.

OAuth.//Audience: The Entra App ID URI, with NO trailing slash — Entra refuses to register one on identifierUris. Deliberately NOT equal to Resource; see docs/runbooks/entra-and-zendesk-oauth.md.
OAuth.//Resource: Published in RFC 9728 and validated against. Keeps the trailing slash, because that is what Claude Code normalises to.
OAuth.//UpstreamResourceScope: Set => the RFC 8707 resource parameter is validated and then terminated here, with this scope naming the API upstream instead. Empty is the RFC 8707 default, relaying the indicator; Entra is the outlier that requires this to be set.

Authorization.//CustomPermissionsClaim: Only consulted when LiveGroupCheck is false. With it true — every deployed target — entitlement comes from Graph alone and no claim can grant access.

Audit.//IncludeReads: Audit reads (GET) as well as mutations. Defaults to TRUE — most tools are reads and this is the only server-side record of who read which ticket. Set false only as a deliberate ingest-cost decision.

//Logging: NOT IN FORCE, and kept only as a shape reference. This file is a template that ASP.NET Core never loads, and a real appsettings.json cannot reach the container anyway - .gitignore and .dockerignore both exclude it. The levels that DO apply are set in Program.cs via builder.Logging.AddFilter, which ships with the image and cannot drift per deployment.
